scope: Proposition 8.6 (Vector estimates on arbitrary inner-valid intervals) of the manuscript “Almost-everywhere Fourier convergence in L log L” (preprints/Almost-everywhere-Fourier-convergence-in-L-log-L-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 075 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 9a77d41e5b9b9beb), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix a live plateau, a main level b ∈ [b0, 1], and a representative s at its snapshot birth. There is a family of predictable estimate origins, containing run starts and the checkpoints described below, whose conditional expected size at the birth is at most P(d, b−1 0 ) for an absolute fixed polynomial P. For every t ≥ 0, outside a conditional event of probability at most CP(d, b−1 0 )e−t, every contiguous interval I of inner-valid jumps after this birth satisfies ∫︂ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ∑︂ p∈I ap(z)ϵj(p)rj(p)+2 ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ dz ≤ C ∑︂ p∈I Jp + Cb−1/2 (1 + Ke + Ee,b) + Cb1/2 t. (8.16) The Fisher sum is taken only over I. The representative remains eligible for these estimates until the plateau ends, even if another snapshot has meanwhile replaced the one at which it was born.
